summary: Conditional civic-letter workflow: real code exists, but demand and deliverability are unvalidated.
adoptionNote: POM soul-review + wrk.dog merge constitute adoption — operator ruling 2026-06-12; see the PR's POM record

operatorContext.registryNote: Personal/research asset, not near-term investible BOS; operator must confirm whether it should pitch as a business. [evidence: dispatch registry note]

methods: Read root and planning soul files where present.
Read representative web, API, worker, Prisma, and test files.
Compared stale planning audit against current worktree shape.
Tagged repo-backed claims as evidence and external/market claims as assumptions.

thesisCurrent.statement: CivicState can become a transactional civic communication product if it proves residents pay $5-$25, official routing works, citations remain safe, and government email delivery clears quality gates. [evidence: BUSINESS.md]
thesisCurrent.confidence: conditional; no live revenue, traffic, or deliverability evidence in workspace [assumption: workspace review]

customerDefinition.primaryCustomer: United States resident with a specific civic frustration who wants the right officials contacted but will not do the research, drafting, and routing manually. [evidence: .planning/GENESIS.md]
excludedCustomers: Legal claimants seeking advice or filings [evidence: .planning/GENESIS.md]
Enterprise advocacy buyers [assumption: current pricing and code are consumer transactional]
Community/social movement users requiring co-signing, comments, or coalition tools [evidence: .planning/GENESIS.md]

marketSizing.knownMarketSize: Unknown; no external research performed. [assumption: network disabled]
marketSizing.method: Bottom-up validation ladder rather than top-down TAM.

validationWedge.claim: Break-even at about $340/month and about 25 Amplify submissions/month.
At the repo's 3% willingness-to-pay gate, about 850 qualified visitors/month are needed for about 25 paid submissions.
Year-one plan scenario is 400 submissions at $18 average order value for $7,200/month.

competition.name: Resistbot
competition.position: Citizen letter tool; CivicState differentiates through research and citations.

competition.name: Change.org
competition.position: Petition hosting; CivicState differentiates through individualized delivery.
competition.honesty: evidence: MASTER_PLAN.md; assumption: not independently verified

competition.name: LegalZoom
competition.position: Document drafting; CivicState differentiates by avoiding legal advice and focusing on civic communication.
competition.honesty: evidence: MASTER_PLAN.md; assumption: not independently verified

competition.name: Quorum / VoterVoice
competition.position: Enterprise advocacy; CivicState targets individual transactional buyers.

risksAntiplan.skepticalView: This may be a useful personal/research demo rather than a business: users may not pay, officials may ignore AI-assisted mail, official data may be sparse, and legal/compliance burden may overwhelm low transaction prices. [assumption: EIR anti-plan from workspace review]
holes: No live revenue or paid conversion evidence. [assumption: workspace review]
No government inbox-placement evidence. [assumption: workspace review]
No official coverage audit by ZIP. [assumption: workspace review]
No independent legal review of disclaimers, AI disclosure, or CAN-SPAM posture. [assumption: workspace review]
mitigations: Run deliverability tests against 85% inbox placement threshold. [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md]
Audit official coverage against 95% federal/state and 60% local thresholds. [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md]
Keep legal advice and filings excluded from scope. [evidence: .planning/GENESIS.md]
residualRisks: Even passing deliverability does not prove officials will respond.
Even passing paid conversion does not prove retention or repeat use.
Even accurate citations may not eliminate legal/compliance risk.

assumptionLedger.assumption: One operator can handle review workload.
assumptionLedger.validation: Flag queue depth and review-time measurement

goToMarket.secondary: Social sharing of public campaign pages [evidence: .planning/GENESIS.md; assumption: no sharing proof]
goToMarket.nearTerm: Manual beta cohort to produce conversion and deliverability evidence [assumption: needed because SEO proof is absent]
